literal: Will renounce indeed, enjoyment those without, things destined to be experienced without feeding will pass if.
translation: Even those without worldly enjoyments would renounce the world, if the experiences destined for them would pass away without forcing themselves upon them.
modern: தாம் அனுபவிக்க வேண்டிய வினைகள் தங்களை அனுபவிக்கச் செய்யாமல் தாமாகவே கழிந்துபோகுமானால், வறுமையில் உள்ளவர்கள் கூட உலக வாழ்க்கையைத் துறந்து விடுவார்கள்.
explanation: This couplet illustrates the inescapable power of destiny. It observes that people who lack wealth and worldly enjoyments ('துப்புரவு இல்லார்') have little reason to remain attached to worldly life, yet they do not easily become ascetics. The reason is that destiny does not simply pass away ('கழியும்'); it actively forces individuals to undergo their allotted experiences ('உறற்பால'). The word 'ஊட்டா' (without feeding) vividly personifies destiny as an entity that insists on feeding people their destined joys and sorrows, thereby keeping even the destitute bound to the world.
